title: The Thirsty Dog
summary: The story of a man who gave water to a thirsty dog, and Allah forgave him, as told by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم. (Bukhari and Muslim)
moral: Be kind to all of Allah's creatures. No good deed, however small, toward a living being is ever wasted with Allah.
pages: That day the desert was very hot. A dog walked weakly, its tongue hanging out, its throat terribly dry. It searched everywhere for water, but did not find a single drop.
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم told of a man who was walking along a road and felt very thirsty. He found a well, climbed down into it, drank his fill, and climbed back up.
When he came out of the well, he saw a dog panting and licking the ground from thirst. The man said to himself, 'This dog is as thirsty as I was.'
So he went back down into the well, filled his leather shoe with water, held it in his mouth, and climbed up. He gave the dog a drink until it was satisfied.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم said, 'Allah thanked him and forgave him.' The companions asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, do we get a reward for being good to animals?' He replied, 'In every living creature with a moist heart there is a reward.'
From this story we learn to love all of Allah's creatures: people, animals, and plants. Even a good deed as small as giving a thirsty dog a drink is rewarded by Allah. The end.
